messages.content: Question 0: tell me about streaming.

Only a couple of decoder layers are resident at any moment. Each decoder layer is copied to the GPU just before it runs and released after. The host keeps the frozen base in pinned memory so copies can overlap compute. Four-bit NF4 weights are dequantised on the card inside each matrix multiply. The adapter is the only part of the model that the optimizer ever updates. Gradient checkpointing recomputes activations instead of keeping them resident. A T4 has no bf16 units, so the run computes in fp16 with a gradient scaler. The scaler skips a step when it sees an overflow and halves its scale. Two buffers let the next layer arrive while the current one is computing. The embedding and the head are large, so they get a slot of their own. Peak memory follows the largest layer, not the size of the whole model. Throughput depends on how much compute each streamed byte is used for. Short sequences leave the card waiting on the copy engine most of the time. Longer sequences give each copied layer more work and raise utilisation. The forecast divides the measured matrix rate by six times the parameter count. Real runs have landed between two thirds of that ceiling and all of it.
